gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-elms-sans: Shantell Sans has a wide, open mouth and one fixed pen width, like a marker doodling a headline. Elms Sans takes over below with a ballpoint's plain line and an s you can see through, keeping the page tidy.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-encode-sans: Encode Sans reads plainly, its c never mistaken for an o. Shantell Sans does the hollow, glass-tube lettering with a constant thickness and a playful wave, while Encode Sans does the quiet, dependable lowercase work underneath.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-encode-sans-expa: Loose, bouncy, a bit cheeky. Shantell Sans skims along on strokes that never change weight, while Encode Sans Expanded does the steadier job of holding its c shapes wide open with the tips pulled apart.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-encode-sans-sc: Playful, first of all. Shantell Sans curves with the heft of a rope, and Encode Sans SC settles in beneath with a shallow terminal curl and a wide gap, giving the page a sensible anchor.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-encode-sans-semi: Hand-drawn and a little goofy up top, with n arches as thick as their stems. Encode Sans Semi Condensed then carries the text, its s opening wide, so paragraphs move along easily.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-exo: That wide mouth, drawn with one fixed nib width and no brush-style swell anywhere, is what you notice first in Shantell Sans. Exo follows with wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp, so paragraphs stay approachable and easy on the eye.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-exo-2: Scribbly and friendly, with no modulation in the stroke from Shantell Sans, then Exo 2 behind it, its curves full of daylight. The strongest quality is that tidy, clear text beside a wobbly marker-like headline.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-faculty-glyphic: Where thin hairline joins would usually sit, Shantell Sans runs full-width stroke connections and a wide, open mouth. Faculty Glyphic keeps its rounded letters clearly open, so a long passage moves along smoothly.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-fahkwang: Fahkwang has a faint nib-pressure variation in each round letter and curves that finish well before they close. And Shantell Sans, with no modulation in its stroke, makes the strongest single quality of this pair a friendly, hand-drawn contrast.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-figtree: A mouth as wide as a tin can's cut lid, drawn at one fixed nib width, defines Shantell Sans. Figtree answers in marker-tip letters with an e open wide at its terminal, and that shared hand-drawn warmth is the pair's strongest quality.
